title: Metabolite Release in Patients with ICU Acquired Weakness
summary:
Acute muscle wasting, which is observed in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit and is estimated at around 2% of muscle mass per day, represents a major clinical challenge. The loss of muscle tissue is often accompanied by other metabolic disorders, which further impairs the patient's condition.
In our observational study, we want to investigate the metabolic changes that occur in critically ill patients. By taking blood samples from arteries and veins, we aim to identify metabolic products that are released from the leg muscles of intensive care patients with muscle atrophy. With this approach, we aim to understand the metabolic pathways involved in muscle wasting and the associated metabolic disorders. Ultimately, findings from our study have the potential to support the development of novel treatments aimed at curbing muscle wasting and correcting metabolic disorders in ICU patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Intensive care treatment, admitted to intensive care unit within the last 24 hours, immobilization and ventilation for at least 48 hours, written consent
Exclusion criteria:
Expected death or termination of life-sustaining measures, femoral venous puncture not feasible, pregnancy
